fields.description: Which of the four shapes decision #10 requires this room is. Set once, at creation: a DM cannot become a group.
fields.label: Room Type

fields.description: Absent for direct messages, which are rendered from the peer's name instead.
fields.label: Title

fields.description: 0 inherits the site-wide setting from Chat Settings.
fields.label: Retention Days

fields.description: Per-document rooms only. Set together with Linked Document or not at all: the unique (linked_doctype, linked_document) constraint hits the empty-string trap if only one is filled.
fields.label: Linked Doctype

fields.description: Direct messages only. The lexicographically LOWER of the pair, so (A,B) and (B,A) resolve to one row under the unique (dm_user_1, dm_user_2) constraint.
fields.label: DM User 1

fields.description: Direct messages only. The lexicographically HIGHER of the pair.
fields.label: DM User 2

fields.description: WHEN the backing Google space is created, not whether the room exists. On First Message is the default because project-wide space writes are capped at 60/minute: eagerly provisioning a space per per-document room would saturate that quota for hours and leave thousands of empty spaces in every coworker's Chat client.
fields.label: Provisioning Mode
fields.options:
Not Mirrored
On Create
On First Message

fields.description: §4.H. WHO decides who is in this room - stated explicitly, never inferred from whichever side changed last, because inferring it is how a membership flaps. Bidirectional accepts a change from either side and reconciles to the union. ERPNext makes the Chat Room Member rows authoritative: a member added in the native Chat client is REVERTED back out on the next reconciliation. That revert is capped by Chat Settings.max_reverts_per_hour and counted in reverts_this_hour, because a person who keeps re-adding themselves and a reconciler that keeps removing them is an infinite loop that burns the 300-per-minute project membership-write quota. Per room, not site-wide: a Document room whose membership is derived from a Project's team and an ad-hoc Group room want opposite answers.
fields.label: Membership Authority

fields.description: Truncated to 1000 characters at write.
fields.label: Provisioning Error

fields.description: OBSERVED FROM GOOGLE, never requested: this space admits members from outside the Workspace domain. §4.H data-egress policy - a room an external participant can read must not be mirrored automatically, because mirroring it sends company conversation to somebody the org chart does not cover. The provisioning sweep and the outbound relay both skip such a room unless Mirror Whitelisted is ticked. Read back on every reconciliation pass rather than cached at creation, because a space can acquire an external member long after we provisioned it.
fields.label: External Users Allowed

fields.description: A human has explicitly approved mirroring this room despite External Users Allowed. The ONLY override, and deliberately a manual tick rather than a rule: the whole point of the external-user gate is that the decision to send company conversation outside the domain belongs to a person, and any rule that could set this automatically would be that decision made by a config field instead. The one field in this section that is not read_only, for exactly that reason.
fields.label: Mirror Whitelisted

fields.description: The Google Chat space resource name, spaces/{space}. Data(255), not the varchar(140) default: Google documents no maximum for the {space} segment, and 255 sits ~3x inside MariaDB's 3072-byte index-key limit under ROW_FORMAT=DYNAMIC. unique on the DocField (never only in a patch) so Frappe coerces the unset value to NULL and unprovisioned rooms can coexist.
fields.label: Google Chat Space Name

fields.description: Read back from spaces.get. spaceThreadingState is Output only on Google's side, so this is observed, never requested.
fields.label: Google Chat Threading State

fields.description: Deep link into the native Google Chat client.
fields.label: Google Chat Space URI

fields.description: THE SEQUENCE ALLOCATOR. outbox.allocate_seq issues UPDATE tabChat Room SET seq_high_water = seq_high_water + 1 WHERE name = %s and reads the value back, both inside the inserting transaction: the UPDATE takes an exclusive lock on this one row, held to commit, which is what makes the read-back safe under concurrency. unique(room, seq) remains the GUARANTEE; this counter is the OPTIMISATION that stops the guarantee ever being tested. Never allocate with MAX(seq) over tabChat Message - that takes range locks across the busiest table in the feature. MAX(seq) is legitimate only as the repair (outbox.repair_seq_high_water) after a collision has already proved the counter is behind. Never move it backwards: ChatRoom.validate refuses, because a decrement re-issues sequence numbers that already exist.
fields.label: Sequence High Water

fields.description: THE RETIREMENT FLOOR, and the mirror of seq_high_water: every message in this room at or below this seq is gone forever, so the room's live range is (retired_below_seq, seq_high_water]. 0 means nothing is retired, which is every room until a purge moves it. Only ever goes UP, and never past seq_high_water — ChatRoom.validate refuses both, because lowering it re-admits derived coverage of messages that no longer exist and nothing can rebuild that coverage correctly, the source being gone. Consumed by the chunk indexer (as a watermark floor, so deleting a room's chunks cannot retreat the watermark and cause the sweep to re-chunk surviving messages verbatim), by the digest sweeps, and by the retrieval gate. The arithmetic lives in chat/retire_rules.py.
fields.label: Retired Below Sequence

fields.description: Denormalised from Chat Message. Written with set_value(update_modified=False) so the room's modified stays meaningful.
fields.label: Last Message

fields.description: When an inbound Google event last touched this room - any event, not only a message. §4.J's reconciliation sweep picks its rooms from the gap between this and last_reconcile_at: a room with recent events and a stale reconcile is where drift is both most likely and cheapest to find, and a room with neither can be skipped for free. Distinct from last_message_at, which moves for our OWN messages too and so cannot answer 'is the inbound pipeline alive for this space'.
fields.label: Last Event At

fields.description: When the §4.J reconciliation sweep last compared this room against Google. Paired with last_event_at and never with modified - modified moves for a dozen reasons that have nothing to do with sync, so scheduling off it would re-reconcile a room because somebody renamed it.
fields.label: Last Reconcile At

fields.description: PLAIN TEXT, truncated to 200 characters, escaped by us. Core Notification Log subjects carry raw HTML and the bell renders it as markup; the room list must not become a second render surface for a message body.
fields.label: Last Message Preview

fields.description: How many membership reverts this room has applied inside the current window (see Revert Window Start). Capped by Chat Settings.max_reverts_per_hour, and THE CAP IS THE POINT: with membership_authority = ERPNext, somebody who keeps re-adding themselves in the native client against a reconciler that keeps removing them is an infinite loop, and each round trip spends the 300-per-minute project membership-write quota that every other room shares. At the cap this room stops reverting and raises an alarm for a human, because two systems disagreeing about who belongs in a room is a question about the org, not a retry.
fields.label: Reverts This Hour

fields.description: Start of the current revert-count window; reverts_this_hour resets when this is more than an hour old. A stored column rather than a Redis counter deliberately: the prod deploy FLUSHDBs Redis, and a loop-breaker that resets on every release is not a loop-breaker - the flap would resume the moment a deploy landed, which is exactly when nobody is watching this field.
fields.label: Revert Window Start
